cohort: 200 pregnant women with BMI between 20-30 kg/m^2, with 100 women in the obese group (BMI 25-30) and 100 women in the non-obese group (BMI 20-24.9).
finding: Obesity during pregnancy is associated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, including a significantly higher rate of instrumental vaginal delivery, caesarian section, and fetal birth asphyxia.
mod_finding: Obese women had a significantly higher rate of instrumental and operative deliveries compared to non-obese women.
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured, with macrosomia defined as 4000g or above.
